concepts.def: How many times bigger the image is than real
Smallest gap two points can have and still be seen
How big the cell looks on screen or paper
True real-life size of the cell
Uses light — cheap, sees living cells, lower detail
Uses electrons — huge magnification, tiny organelles

walkthroughs.body_html:
Magnification = image size ÷ actual size

Rearrange it like a triangle:

- Actual size = image ÷ magnification
- Image size = magnification × actual

Keep units the same on top and bottom. If image is in mm, convert actual to mm first.

A cell looks 5 mm wide on screen. The real cell is 50 µm wide.

Step 1: same units. 5 mm = 5000 µm.

Step 2: divide. 5000 ÷ 50 = ×100 magnification.

Light microscope: cheap, sees colour and living cells, max ~×2000.

Electron microscope: much higher resolution — shows tiny organelles like ribosomes. But expensive, and only dead samples.

A scale bar on an image tells you what one real length looks like. Measure the bar in mm, then use the magnification formula.
